summary: Phase-32 rev-4 — Auto-retry on Order ID collisions for AUTO-GENERATED ids in POST /api/shipments and POST /api/orders/pending/{id}/ship. Both retry paths verified end-to-end against the live backend. 6 new tests + 5 regression tests (rev-3) all PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: shipments_write.py file is 1410 lines — exceeds 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into create / cancel / ship_pending modules in a future iteration.

Duplicate-key detection uses string matching on `'duplicate key' in str(e).lower()` / `'E11000' in str(e)`. Works but a typed pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError check would be more robust. Not a blocker.
seed_data_creation: Per-test seed shipments inserted directly into Mongo (collision trap) and cleaned up in the same test. Wallet topped up to 100000 credits for user2 in autouse fixture to avoid 402 masking.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Tests A2/B2 use a far-future fake YYMMDD prefix (`991231`) for the colliding autogen id so it cannot match the live counter's current sequence (which uses today's IST date). For A2 the seed shipment is inserted with `master_order_id=''` so the in-handler pre-check on master_order_id does NOT pre-empt — the duplicate fires at the actual `db.shipments.insert_one(doc)` site, exercising the retry-on-DuplicateKeyError loop. For B2 the pre-alloc loop in ship_pending_order detects the collision via `find_one({order_id, user_id})` against shipments, regenerates, and updates the pending row before insert. Both verified to return regenerated ids != original.
rca_of_issue: N/A — this iteration verified the implemented fix. RCA from prior iterations: pymongo DuplicateKeyError on compound unique index (order_id, user_id) was surfacing as 500 (rev-3 made it 409) but for AUTO-GENERATED ids the operator should never see any error — rev-4 wraps both inserts in retry-on-DuplicateKeyError loops (5 retries), regenerating via generate_master_order_id() on each attempt, only when the id was server-allocated (auto_gen=True AND order_id == master_order_id). User-typed / external order_ids still surface 409 cleanly.
